document_check.note: The document is Yakoub Y et al. 'Plasma p-tau217 identifies cognitively normal older adults who will develop cognitive impairment in a 10-year window', Alzheimer's & Dementia 2025;21:e14537 (PREVENT-AD cohort). It reports Cox HR 7.81 (95% CI 3.92 to 15.59) for A+T+ plasma vs A-T- plasma for progression from cognitively unimpaired to MCI, as cited.

cited_result: Association of plasma amyloid/tau status (A+T+ by plasma Abeta42/40 and p-tau217, vs A-T-) with progression from cognitively unimpaired to MCI: Cox HR 7.81 (3.92 to 15.59), n=215, 16 of 21 A+T+ progressed.
tool_reason: The cited result is the association of one prognostic factor (baseline plasma A/T biomarker status) with a later outcome (incident MCI), estimated as a hazard ratio. It is not a multivariable prediction model and not a causal exposure effect.

domains.rationale: The source population is described: a volunteer longitudinal cohort of people with a first-degree family history of AD. Inclusion required available plasma biomarkers and at least one year of cognitive follow-up after the biomarker time point, which selects on post-baseline follow-up. The main text does not say what proportion of the eligible PREVENT-AD cohort was included (only a supplementary figure). Sample counts are inconsistent: 228 participants are reported in Results, against 215 in the plasma sample.

signalling.question: Is the source population adequately described?
signalling.quote: We included 215 participants from the Presymptomatic Evaluation of Experimental or Novel Treatments for Alzheimer Disease (PREVENT- AD) cohort, a longitudinal observational study of individuals with a first-degree family history of AD (Figure S1 in supporting information).

signalling.question: Is there adequate participation in the study by eligible persons (proportion of the eligible cohort included)?
signalling.quote: Searched Methods and Results for the number of PREVENT-AD participants screened, eligible or excluded; the main text only points to 'Figure S1 in supporting information'.

signalling.question: Are inclusion and exclusion criteria adequately described?
signalling.quote: Participants included in this study were CU based on an extensive neuropsychological evaluation at the time of the biomarker assessment and had a minimum of 1 year of cognitive follow-up thereafter.

signalling.question: Is the baseline study sample adequately described, with consistent numbers?
signalling.quote: A total of 228 participants were included in the study, of whom 62 (27%) developed MCI.

domains.rationale: Follow-up length is reported (mean 5.65 years after plasma classification, range 1.01 to 10.47), and censoring is handled in the Cox model. The number lost to follow-up, the reasons, and any comparison of those lost with those retained are not reported. Informative censoring (for example drop-out from decline, or follow-up during the pandemic) cannot be assessed.

signalling.question: Is the proportion of the baseline sample lost to follow-up, and the reasons, reported?
signalling.quote: Searched Results and figure legends for numbers withdrawn or lost and reasons; only 'The vertical ticks on the curves refer to censored participants, that is, the lack of follow-up of the individuals.'

signalling.question: Is the length of follow-up adequate and reported?
signalling.quote: The mean cognitive follow-up was 5.65 years (SD = 1.45, range 1.01–10.47) after plasma classification

signalling.question: Are participants lost to follow-up compared with those who completed?
signalling.quote: Searched Results and Discussion for a comparison of participants with short versus complete follow-up; none reported.

signalling.question: Could events during follow-up have influenced ascertainment?
signalling.quote: Finally, part of the study follow-up occurred during the COVID-19 pandemic, which may have contributed to the development or deterioration of cognitive impairment.

domains.rationale: Plasma p-tau217 and Abeta42/40 were measured with established laboratory methods (an in-house Simoa assay; IP-MS) in one laboratory. The binary thresholds were set in advance, independently of the MCI outcome: 2 SD above Abeta-PET-negative CU participants, and a pre-established Abeta42/40 cut-off of 0.09. Which plasma time point was used differed by PET availability. Laboratory blinding to outcome is not reported, but the measures are objective assays.

signalling.question: Is the prognostic factor clearly defined and measured with a valid and reliable method?
signalling.quote: Plasma Aβ40 and Aβ42 concentrations were measured using ultrasensitive immunoprecipitation coupled with mass spectrometry (IP-MS) technique

signalling.question: Are cut-offs for the prognostic factor defined independently of the outcome?
signalling.quote: We used the pre-established thresholds of 0.09 for plasma Aβ42/40 and 0.072 for CSF Aβ42/40.

signalling.question: Is the same method and setting of measurement used for all participants?
signalling.quote: For individuals who did not have PET scans, the plasma sample closest to 2017 was taken.

signalling.question: Was the prognostic factor measured without knowledge of the outcome?
signalling.quote: Searched section 2.1 for whether laboratory staff were masked to clinical status; not reported.

domains.rationale: MCI had an explicit definition: an objective RBANS or RAVLT deficit plus a complaint or observed decline. It was classified by multidisciplinary consensus, blind to plasma, CSF, PET, MRI and APOE, using the same procedure for everyone.

signalling.question: Is the outcome clearly defined?
signalling.quote: In addition to an objective impairment on the RBANS or the RAVLT, to be classified as MCI, participants needed to have a subjective memory complaint21 and/or have an objective decline witnessed over multiple cognitive follow-ups.

signalling.question: Is the outcome measured without knowledge of the prognostic factor?
signalling.quote: All MCI classification was performed blind to plasma, CSF, PET, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and apolipoprotein E (APOE) genotype information.

signalling.question: Is the same method and setting of outcome measurement used for all participants?
signalling.quote: MCI classification was determined in a reserch setting based on a multidisciplinary consensus meeting comprising dementia specialist neuropsychologists (SV and MM) and physicians (SD and MG).

domains.rationale: Age, sex, education and APOE e4 were measured (Table 1). The sentence on covariates is ambiguous about whether the Cox model behind the HR of 7.81 was adjusted for age, sex and education or only the mixed models were; the figure legend puts the covariates with the linear mixed models. APOE e4 was not adjusted for. Age is a strong determinant of both p-tau217 and incident MCI.

signalling.question: Are important potential confounders measured?
signalling.quote: APOE ε4 carriers, n (%) 88 (41)

signalling.question: Are important potential confounders accounted for in the analysis of the cited HR?
signalling.quote: Cox proportional hazard models were used to assess the risk of MCI progression by AT group and linear mixed models were used to assess longitudinal cognitive changes across the biomarker groups with the addition of age at the biomarker classification, sex, and years of education as covariates.

signalling.question: Is APOE genotype accounted for?
signalling.quote: Searched section 2.3 and figure legends for APOE as a model covariate; covariates named are age, sex and years of education only.

domains.rationale: The Cox model suits time to MCI, and HRs are reported with CIs and model concordance. Results are reported for every A/T group, including null contrasts, so selective reporting is not evident. The A+T+ group is small (21 participants, 16 events), and the authors warn that the HRs are imprecise; that is mainly a matter of precision, not direction of bias. A proportional-hazards check is not reported.

signalling.question: Is there sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis?
signalling.quote: [HR] = 7.81, P < 0.001, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 3.92 to 15.59

signalling.question: Is the statistical model adequate for the design?
signalling.quote: Cox proportional hazard models were used to assess the risk of MCI progression by AT group

signalling.question: Is there no selective reporting of results?
signalling.quote: There were no differences between A+T−plasma and A−T−plasma group (HR = 1.14, P = 0.69, 95% CI = 0.58 to 2.24).

signalling.question: Are the numbers of participants and events in the prognostic-factor groups adequate?
signalling.quote: The low sample size in the A+T+ and the A−T+ groups should also be noted.

applicability.rationale: The cohort is enriched for family history of AD and is 98% White and 72% female, with mean age about 65 at biomarker classification: 'One main limitation is the low racial, ethnic (98% White), and sex imbalance (72% female) of our population' (p10). It is not a general community population.
The factor is combined plasma A/T status using an in-house Gothenburg Simoa p-tau217 assay and a cohort-specific threshold (3.98 pg/mL), not a commercial single-marker cut-off.
Research-consensus MCI in cognitively unimpaired people matches the review's outcome of progression from normal cognition to MCI.

overall: High risk of bias. QUIPS: three domains at moderate risk (participation, attrition, confounding); prognostic factor measurement, outcome measurement and analysis are low risk.
overall_rationale: By this review's QUIPS rule, three or more moderate domains give an overall high rating. Participation is moderate: a selected volunteer family-history cohort, inclusion conditioned on at least one year of follow-up, participation proportion not reported, and inconsistent counts. Attrition is moderate: loss to follow-up and reasons not reported. Confounding is moderate: it is ambiguous whether the Cox HR is adjusted, and APOE was not adjusted. The strengths are real (blinded consensus outcome, prespecified thresholds), but the three moderate domains mean the magnitude of HR 7.81 should be treated cautiously.
